t: Minimum Initial Strength to Defeat All Monsters
o: We fight monsters left to right with a strength pool that only decreases (clamped at 0). A boost range adds a temporary bonus used **only** for the feasibility check at that index, never subtracted from the pool. In Example 1, starting with 30: after monster 0 we have 25, the boost lets us pass monster 1 leaving 15, and 15 exactly beats monster 2. In Example 2, overlapping boosts stack (10+5=15), letting a tiny initial 5 survive because the pool hits 0 but the bonus covers everything. Constraints (n, boosts up to 5·10⁴) demand better than O(n·B): aggregate boosts with a difference array, then evaluate feasibility in O(n). Feasibility is monotone in the initial strength, which opens the door to binary search.
k: Aggregate range bonuses with a difference array in O(n + B).
Feasibility is monotone: if strength s works, any s' > s works, so binary search applies.
Because the pool clamps at 0, the closed-form threshold is: for each i with bonus_i < monsters[i], we need s >= (prefix sum before i) + monsters[i] - bonus_i.

a.n: Approach 1: Binary Search on the Answer
a.i: Define feasible(s): simulate with initial strength s, checking cur + bonus >= monsters[i] and updating cur = max(0, cur - monsters[i]). If s works, any larger s also works (every intermediate value only grows), so we can binary search s in [0, sum(monsters)].
s: Build bonus[i] for every index using a difference array over boosts.
Binary search the smallest s such that the O(n) simulation succeeds.
a.t: O((n + B) log S) where S = sum of monsters — each feasibility check is O(n) and we do O(log S) of them; difference-array build is O(n + B).
a.sp: O(n) for the bonus prefix array.

a.i: At index i the pool equals max(0, s - P_i) where P_i is the prefix sum of monsters before i. If the bonus alone covers the monster (bonus_i >= monsters[i]), any s passes this index. Otherwise we need s - P_i >= monsters[i] - bonus_i, i.e. s >= P_i + monsters[i] - bonus_i (which automatically exceeds P_i, so the clamp is inactive). Taking the maximum requirement over all indices gives the exact answer in one pass.
s: Compute prefix sums P_i and per-index bonuses via a difference array.
For each i with bonus_i < monsters[i], candidate = P_i + monsters[i] - bonus_i.
Answer is the maximum candidate (0 if none).
a.t: O(n + B) — one difference-array pass plus one linear scan.

w: In an interview, lead with binary search (easy to argue correctness), then present the closed form as the optimization. Pitfalls: forgetting the clamp-at-0 behavior (a naive 'no-clamp' formula overcounts, e.g. Example 1 needs 30, not 15), using 32-bit integers (sums reach 5·10¹³), and off-by-one in the difference array (r+1). Follow-ups: what if boosts expire after use, or if you may reorder monsters?
